findings.statement: The valid fixture's packed layout is internally consistent: outer entries are tag + 32-bit pointer (5 bytes), conditional entries are two 16-bit operands + pointer (8 bytes), and the native bytewise pointer reader handles the unaligned pointer positions. The two tables have different zero-terminator widths.
findings.resolution: Accept the exact CLI/GNU ARM witness for these fixture bytes, labels, and relocations only; do not extend it to ROM/runtime or malformed-input safety.

findings.statement: Poryscript's parser chooses direct versus table syntax from punctuation and appends any identifier as the map-script type; it does not check that table syntax is restricted to FireRed's table types or that direct syntax is not used for them. It also has no duplicate-type rejection. The FireRed consumer dispatches type 2 and type 4 through the conditional-table reader, while direct types are run as script bytecode; duplicate outer tags resolve to the first match.
findings.resolution: Keep as a confirmed source-level producer/consumer contract objection. Require parser-level type-shape and duplicate-tag rejection (or a source-backed proof of intended semantics) before approving the parser/emitter contract. No upstream pin was changed.

findings.statement: The conditional reader treats a zero first 16-bit operand as the table sentinel. Poryscript parses and emits the operand text without rejecting zero, so a table entry beginning with zero is indistinguishable from termination and later entries are unreachable.
findings.resolution: Keep as a source-level objection. Add an actual-CLI negative fixture and either reject zero as the first operand or document and verify a valid alternate encoding; no such run occurred in this review.

findings.statement: Neither native reader has a table length, end pointer, or bounds check. Missing sentinels, truncated records, or invalid relocated pointers can advance/read past the table; the host bounded decoder and compile-time mutation controls do not establish native safety.
findings.resolution: No resolution claimed. Requires a separate native execution or bounded-container contract; preserve as unresolved evidence.

findings.statement: FireRed's preprocessor converts Poryscript's double-colon labels to GAS-compatible global labels. The root Makefile routes .s data through preproc, CPP, enum-enabled preproc, and ARM assembler; mapjson emits a MapHeader pointer to the map's MapScripts label. The actual-CLI witness uses the pinned preprocessor and native macro bodies but does not insert output into that full root build.
findings.resolution: Accept the observed preprocessing dependency and map-header ownership link. Full Poryscript CLI-to-Makefile/ROM integration remains unproven.

file_verdicts.basis: The scoped parser lines confirm the type-shape, duplicate-tag, and zero-sentinel objections, but this is not a whole-file semantic disposition and the actual CLI negative cases were not run.
The map-table writer and generated-label ranges are source-anchored, but a full emitter review and actual-CLI malformed-input controls are outstanding.
Generated chunk labels and entrypoint scope were inspected for ownership only; full control-flow emission semantics were not reviewed.
CLI parse-to-emitter flow and default optimization/line-marker flags were inspected; complete CLI configuration behavior was not reviewed.
Both relevant macro bodies were verified; unrelated map/event macros and the full file's contracts were not dispositioned.
The full map-script table reader and callers were traced; the remaining file was not reviewed as a whole and native malformed-input safety is unresolved.
The bytewise T1/T2 read macros were verified to interpret the packed little-endian pointers; the rest of the header was not reviewed.
All type constants were read and matched to the consumers, but this proposal is not registered as a whole-file approval.
